indicator_definition: Energy productivity measures how much economic output is generated per unit of energy consumed. It is calculated as GDP divided by gross inland energy consumption and expressed in euros per kilogram of oil equivalent (EUR/kgoe). A higher value indicates more efficient use of energy to generate economic output.
rationale: Improving energy productivity is central to decoupling economic growth from energy consumption and reducing environmental pressures. More productive use of energy lowers costs for businesses and households and reduces emissions. Progress means a sustained increase in energy productivity over time.
methodology_characteristics: Energy productivity is calculated by Eurostat using GDP data (chain-linked volumes, reference year 2010) and gross inland energy consumption from national energy balances. Both indicators are compiled under EU energy statistics regulations. Data are published annually.
